summary: LunaView is an interactive lunar mission planning application developed to support the rapid evaluation and comparison of potential lunar landing sites. It integrates scientific data and computational tools to help users assess the suitability of different locations on the Moon. The application features interactive landing site selection, site comparison, solar illumination analysis, mission window calculations, and 360° terrain horizon analysis using Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data. By combining lunar terrain information with astronomical and environmental calculations, LunaView provides insights into sunlight availability, surrounding terrain obstacles, and potential landing conditions. This addresses the challenge of making lunar landing site assessments more accessible, efficient, and data-driven. The project is important because selecting a suitable landing site is essential for mission safety, operational planning, and scientific success, particularly for future lunar exploration missions that require reliable access to sunlight, safe terrain, and sustainable surface operations.
details:
LunaView is an interactive lunar mission planning application designed to help researchers, engineers, and mission planners rapidly evaluate and compare potential lunar landing sites. The application brings together lunar terrain data, astronomical calculations, and interactive visualizations to support more informed decisions about future lunar exploration.

How It Works

Users can select and compare different lunar landing sites, including historically significant and potential future landing locations. LunaView analyses several important mission factors, including solar illumination conditions, mission windows, and surrounding terrain. Using Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data from NASA, the application performs 360° terrain horizon analysis to identify surrounding obstacles and assess how local topography may affect sunlight visibility. Astronomical calculations using NASA/JPL SPICE resources support solar position and mission planning assessments. Results are presented through an interactive dashboard to make complex scientific information easier to understand.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LunaView reduces the effort required to evaluate lunar landing locations by bringing multiple assessment capabilities into one accessible platform. It helps users understand terrain characteristics, identify potential illumination constraints, compare landing site conditions, and explore suitable mission planning opportunities. Its intended impact is to support safer, more efficient, and data-driven lunar mission planning while making lunar science and exploration analysis more accessible to students, researchers, and the wider space community.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using:

  • Python: Main programming language for scientific calculations and application development.
  • Streamlit: Interactive web application framework and dashboard interface.
  • NumPy: Numerical and scientific computations.
  • Rasterio and GDAL: Processing and analysing lunar elevation raster datasets.
  • pyproj: Coordinate transformations and geospatial calculations.
  • SpiceyPy and NASA/JPL SPICE: Astronomical and planetary geometry calculations.
  • NASA LOLA datasets: Lunar elevation and terrain information.
  • GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud: Source code management, collaboration, and application deployment.

The project is software-based and does not require specialised physical hardware beyond a computer and internet access.

Creativity and Innovation

LunaView's creativity lies in integrating several complex lunar mission assessment functions into a single interactive planning environment. Instead of treating terrain, sunlight, and mission timing as separate problems, the application combines them to provide a more comprehensive understanding of landing site suitability. Its 360° terrain horizon analysis adds an important local perspective by considering how surrounding topography can obstruct sunlight, rather than relying solely on the general solar elevation angle. The interactive design also allows users to explore different sites and compare results without needing to operate multiple specialised scientific tools independently.

Factors Considered by the Team

During development, the team considered scientific accuracy, data availability, computational efficiency, usability, and practical mission requirements. Particular attention was given to:

  • Lunar terrain elevation and surface characteristics.
  • Solar illumination and potential periods of darkness.
  • Surrounding terrain obstacles and horizon visibility.
  • Mission timing and suitable operational windows.
  • Reliable use of NASA scientific datasets and astronomical resources.
  • Efficient processing of large geospatial datasets.
  • Accessibility through a clear and interactive interface.
  • Reliability and performance when deployed as a web application.

Ultimately, LunaView aims to transform complex lunar scientific data into useful, understandable information that can contribute to better-informed decisions for future lunar exploration.
